messages.text: 'Bullied' and 'out of control' - Chelsea's defensive issues laid bare

metadata.summary: "You need to feel it. We're not feeling it," said Xabi Alonso after Chelsea's 3-0 loss at Brentford. Yet Chelsea are stuck in a familiar feeling.
metadata.content: Brentford 3-0 Chelsea: Defensive issues for Xabi Alonso laid bare after chastening west London derby defeat | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Brentford 3-0 Chelsea: Defensive issues for Xabi Alonso laid bare after chastening west London derby defeat Chelsea well beaten 3-0 by Brentford after dismal second half in the west London derby; Xabi Alonso's side continue to fail to keep clean sheets, concede from set-pieces and lack 'competitive mentality' when they fall behind; Chelsea now winless in three league games after a good start Sam Blitz Football Journalist @SamBIitz Saturday 19 September 2026 07:07, UK Image: Chelsea players stand dejected after conceding the third goal against Brentford "You need to feel it. We're not feeling it," said Xabi Alonso after Chelsea's 3-0 loss at Brentford. Yet Chelsea are stuck in a familiar feeling. Another defeat, their 11th of the calendar year - more than they had in 2025, with three months of this year to go. At least two goals conceded for the fifth straight Premier League game under Alonso. More set-piece woe. "We dropped our consistency, our competitive mentality needed in the second half," said Alonso. That will concern Chelsea fans the most. It was way too easy for Brentford to take over that second half. And there's another continuing trend: Chelsea being outbattled in a match. Remember, they were outrun in the vast majority of their Premier League matches last season. Transfer Centre LIVE! | Chelsea news

metadata.summary: When Wakefield Trinity came back into Super League for the 2025 season, there wouldn't have been many who would have foreseen a semi-final appearance within two seasons- except those in their inner sanctum.

When Wakefield Trinity came back into Super League for the 2025 season, there wouldn't have been many who would have foreseen a semi-final appearance within two seasons- except those in their inner sanctum. That inner sanctum, among others, consists of owner Matt Ellis, head of recruitment Ste Mills, and head coach Daryl Powell. Working in tandem, they came up with a plan for how they would continually progress: they have signed raw talent, made them stars, provided a stadium that both home and away fans enjoy attending, and now brought the progressive and rapid success that their most faithful have been waiting so long to see.
